title: Induction principle for separated quasi-compact opens
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let P be a property of quasi-compact open subschemes of X. Assume P holds for every affine open, and assume that whenever U is quasi-compact open and V is affine open, P holds for U, V, and U intersect V, then P holds for U union V. Then P holds for every separated quasi-compact open subscheme W of X.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 08DR (coherent-lemma-induction-principle), proof, first induction for separated quasi-compact opens

proof.text: Let W be a separated quasi-compact open subscheme of X. By the finite-affine-cover statement, choose a finite affine open cover W = U_1 \cup \cdots \cup U_n. Induct on n. For n > 1 set U = U_1 \cup \cdots \cup U_{n-1} and V = U_n. Since W is separated over Spec Z, the affine-intersection statement applied with A = Z shows that each U_i \cap V is affine; hence U \cap V is a finite union of affine opens and is quasi-compact. The inclusions U \hookrightarrow W and U \cap V \hookrightarrow W are open immersions and therefore separated by separated cancellation, while W \to Spec Z is separated; separatedness of composites makes U and U \cap V separated.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 08DR (coherent-lemma-induction-principle), proof, first paragraph (separated quasi-compact opens)

proof.text: The case n = 1 is the affine hypothesis. For n > 1, the induction hypothesis applies to the separated quasi-compact opens U and U \cap V, and the affine hypothesis applies to V. The assumed gluing implication for U and V therefore gives P(U \cup V) = P(W). This proves P(W) for every separated quasi-compact open W.
